answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region, so shifting traffic off that region is the intervention that can restore availability without reverting the mandated security patch or shedding customer writes. Rollback is ruled out by compliance (and memory_b1 is therefore not actionable). Circuit breaking (memory_b4) fails fast and would drop settlement writes, which violates the objective. Replica routing (memory_b5) previously helped when dashboard/report reads sat on the primary; today’s load is peak settlement writes, so that mechanism is a weak match. Adding capacity (memory_b3) absorbed a surge when headroom was provisioned before the peak, not after 90 minutes of 5x write latency. memory_b2 is the closest prior (clean regional shift, latency and errors recovered in minutes) but it is not the same write-intensity context, so I am verifying that record and would fail over as a controlled standard cutover rather than an unguarded dump. Cause remains uncertain (release vs regional saturation vs both); failover treats the observed regional blast radius. Downstream settlement consistency/duplication risk is flagged.
